newsitem.title: UK: Autostrade to launch lira Eurobond next week - Chase.
newsitem.headline: Autostrade to launch lira Eurobond next week - Chase.

text.p: Italy's Autostrade will launch its long-awaited 500 billion lire five-year floating-rate note next week, lead manager Chase said on Monday.
"It will probably launch next Thursday (April 3)," head of new issues Edward Villiers at Chase said.
"It has already seen interest from institutional investors, bank and retail investors in continental Europe."
Credito Italiano is joint lead manager for the transaction.

Villiers said the deal was likely to pay a coupon of three- month LIBOR plus 20 basis points with an issue and reoffer price of par. There will be call options in years three and four at par. The bond will be listed in Luxemburg and governed by English law.

Villiers said investors would be subject to the same tax laws as those which apply to Italian government bonds, BTPs. Under the structure, holders will receive gross coupon payments as long as they can prove eligibility.
Autostrade announced that it would launch the deal in October last year. At the time it said the bulk of the money would be used to cancel previous debts. Autostrade is unrated.
Autostrade was the first borrower to tap the international bond markets in 1963, with a $15 million offering via SG Warburg, now SBC Warburg.
The company has recently been more active in the syndicated loan market.
